asset_name: Guselkumab (TREMFYA) treatment persistence in psoriatic arthritis
mechanism: Human IgG1 lambda monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the p19 subunit of interleukin-23 and inhibits IL-23 receptor interaction, reducing downstream inflammatory cytokine signaling.
development_status: Not a pipeline development asset. NCT07532226 (PEGASUS) is a recruiting, prospective observational cohort study of routine-practice guselkumab persistence in adults with psoriatic arthritis in France; no drug is provided as part of the study. TREMFYA is already approved and marketed for active psoriatic arthritis.
expected_launch_window: Already launched/approved for active psoriatic arthritis
clinical_summary: PEGASUS is designed to measure real-world persistence, discontinuation, reasons for switching, disease activity, enthesitis, pain, patient impact, satisfaction, and safety outcomes over up to 24 months in about 200 participants starting guselkumab according to the local SmPC. It is not a registrational efficacy trial. Marketed TREMFYA demonstrated higher ACR20 response than placebo at Week 24 in two pivotal PsA trials, with q8w dosing after starter doses and use alone or with conventional DMARDs.
safety_summary: NCT07532226 collects adverse events, serious adverse events, infections, injection-site reactions, and tolerability over up to 2 years in routine practice. The approved label warns about serious hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis, infections, TB evaluation, possible hepatotoxicity monitoring, and avoiding live vaccines; common adverse reactions in plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis include upper respiratory infections, headache, injection-site reactions, arthralgia, bronchitis, diarrhea, gastroenteritis, tinea infections, and herpes simplex infections.
management_tools: Treat as an already marketed specialty biologic rather than a pipeline launch candidate
Prior authorization requiring active psoriatic arthritis diagnosis and specialist prescribing
Step therapy or sequencing criteria against TNF inhibitors and IL-17A inhibitors where consistent with plan policy
Quantity limits aligned to approved PsA dosing: 100 mg at Weeks 0 and 4, then every 8 weeks
Baseline TB screening and active infection exclusion before treatment
Hepatitis screening, pregnancy counseling, and vaccination review including avoidance of live vaccines
Continuation criteria tied to clinical response, tolerability, and absence of serious infection or unacceptable toxicity
evidence_gaps: NCT07532226 has no posted results and is designed to measure persistence rather than establish new efficacy.
The assigned trial is observational, not FDA-regulated as a drug trial, and states no drug will be provided as part of the study.
French routine-practice persistence results may not generalize directly to U.S. payer management.
No manufacturer WAC disclosure for the 100 mg PsA presentation was located in this search; annual cost uses current U.S. cash/discount price sources and label dosing.
The assigned asset is already approved/marketed for psoriatic arthritis, so it should be considered an exclusion concern for a pipeline-only dashboard.

sources.title: A Study of Guselkumab Treatment Persistence in Psoriatic Arthritis Participants
supports: Official title: A Real-World, Prospective Study of Guselkumab Treatment Persistence in Psoriatic Arthritis Patients
Sponsor Janssen-Cilag Ltd.; acronym PEGASUS
Recruiting observational prospective cohort study; estimated enrollment 200
Actual start date 2026-04-17; estimated primary and study completion 2029-12-10
Primary outcomes assess proportion still receiving treatment at 1 year, persistence time, and new treatment starts
Arm description states no drug will be provided and only routine clinical practice data will be collected
ClinicalTrials.gov oversight lists the study as not FDA-regulated drug or device

sources.title: J&J Study NCT07532226
supports: J&J trial page identifies NCT07532226 and internal study ID CNTO1959PSA4021
Describes the study objective as assessing 1-year persistence of guselkumab in adults with psoriatic arthritis
Mirrors recruiting status, France location, observational design, and routine-practice data collection

sources.title: TREMFYA (guselkumab) Prescribing Information
supports: TREMFYA is indicated for adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg with active psoriatic arthritis
PsA dose is 100 mg subcutaneous injection at Week 0, Week 4, and every 8 weeks thereafter, alone or with a conventional DMARD
Mechanism is selective binding to IL-23 p19 and inhibition of IL-23 receptor interaction
Warnings and precautions include hypersensitivity, infections, TB, hepatotoxicity, and immunizations
Adult PsA studies PsA1 and PsA2 enrolled 1120 adults and showed greater ACR20 response versus placebo at Week 24

sources.title: TREMFYA (guselkumab) Approved by U.S. Food and Drug Administration as the First Selective Interleukin (IL)-23 Inhibitor for Active Psoriatic Arthritis
supports: Janssen announced FDA approval for adult active psoriatic arthritis on 2020-07-14
Approval was based on two pivotal Phase 3 trials
Company described q8w dosing after starter doses and use alone or with conventional DMARDs

sources.title: Tremfya European Medicines Agency EPAR
supports: EMA lists Tremfya as used for psoriatic arthritis in adults, alone or with methotrexate, after disease-modifying medicines have not worked well enough or caused unacceptable side effects
EMA overview describes prefilled syringe or pen use for plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis
EMA describes the active substance as guselkumab and its IL-23 blocking mechanism

sources.title: Tremfya (guselkumab): Uses, Side Effects, Dosage & More
supports: GoodRx listed 100 mg/mL Tremfya injection price as low as $13,364.33 and 100 mg/mL syringe price as low as $13,358.97
GoodRx described typical PsA dosing as 100 mg at Week 0, Week 4, and every 8 weeks from Week 12 onward
GoodRx notes Tremfya is used for active psoriatic arthritis

sources.title: How Much Is Tremfya Without Insurance?
supports: GoodRx reported the list price was $13,873 per dose as of September 2024
GoodRx listed average retail prices of $18,742.88 for the 100 mg/mL One-Press injector and $18,664.95 for the 100 mg/mL prefilled syringe
GoodRx reported that most health plans require prior authorization for Tremfya and that step therapy is common in multiple plan types
GoodRx stated no Tremfya biosimilar is available in the U.S.

sources.title: Guselkumab (TREMFYA) in Psoriatic Arthritis Criteria for Use
supports: VA criteria require prescribing and monitoring by a rheumatologist, dermatologist, or locally designated expert
Criteria require FDA-approved PsA dosing and diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis with inflammatory articular disease
Criteria require TB and hepatitis screening
Criteria include exclusion for active serious infection, untreated TB, certain hepatitis B statuses without prophylaxis, untreated HIV, and live or live-attenuated vaccines near initiation
Criteria require inadequate, inadvisable, or not tolerated TNF inhibitor and IL-17A inhibitor before guselkumab

sources.title: Guselkumab (Tremfya) - Medical Clinical Policy Bulletins
supports: Aetna policy lists active psoriatic arthritis as a covered indication for eligible adults and pediatric patients
Aetna summarizes adult PsA approval in July 2020 and pivotal DISCOVER-1/DISCOVER-2 evidence in 1120 adults
Policy supports payer management through indication-specific coverage criteria

expected_launch_window.value: Already launched/approved for active psoriatic arthritis
expected_launch_window.method: Used FDA/Janssen approval announcement and current U.S. prescribing information instead of forecasting a future launch.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The assigned study evaluates persistence for an already approved product in routine practice. It should not be modeled as a future pipeline launch.

annual_cost_range.method: Applied U.S. cash/discount prices to approved PsA dosing. Low uses GoodRx 100 mg/mL syringe price as low as $13,358.97 multiplied by 6.5 q8w maintenance doses per year. High uses GoodRx average retail price for 100 mg/mL One-Press injector of $18,742.88 multiplied by 8 first-year doses at Weeks 0, 4, 12, 20, 28, 36, 44, and 52.
annual_cost_range.explanation: No direct current WAC disclosure for the 100 mg PsA presentation was found. The range estimates gross annual drug exposure before rebates, discounts, copay assistance, administration costs, or patient cost-sharing.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted approved IL-23 p19 mechanism, established PsA efficacy, q8w dosing, and persistence-study relevance against crowded PsA biologic options and the absence of new PEGASUS efficacy results.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Guselkumab has established efficacy and convenient maintenance dosing, but the assigned trial is post-market persistence research rather than a new mechanism, formulation, or registrational expansion.

budget_impact.method: Combined chronic biologic use, high per-patient annual cost, no U.S. biosimilar, and broad psoriatic arthritis eligibility while accounting for existing PA/step management.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-patient annual drug cost is high and treatment can be chronic, but this is existing spend rather than a new launch budget shock.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed assigned trial design, product market status, existing payer controls, and lack of new approval-seeking endpoint.
disruption_risk.explanation: PEGASUS may inform persistence assumptions but should not materially disrupt formulary operations because guselkumab is already managed as a marketed PsA biologic.

recommended_action.method: Mapped marketed-product observational evidence to monitoring rather than pipeline preparation.
recommended_action.explanation: Track PEGASUS results for persistence and continuation criteria calibration, but do not create launch readiness work for a product already approved in PsA.
